resources.string: Welcome to Sommelle
Sommelle guides you using the first-line recommended method for insomnia: cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I).
The goal: spend less time awake in bed so your sleep becomes deep and continuous again, then gradually lengthen your nights week after week.
The program takes 1 observation week followed by 6 program weeks: each morning you log your night in 20 seconds, and each week Sommelle adjusts your schedule.
Sommelle is a support tool, not a medical device, and it does not replace medical advice. Your data stays on your phone (no account, nothing is sent).
It takes some effort: the diary every morning and, depending on your answers, a tighter sleep window that can make you more tired at first.
Get started

The full program is right for you

1. Week 1 (observation): sleep as usual and log your night each morning.\n2. Weeks 2 to 7 (consolidation): Sommelle temporarily matches your time in bed to your actual sleep time to make it deep and continuous. The first 10 to 15 days cause temporary daytime tiredness (like muscle soreness when resuming exercise): this is the sign that sleep pressure is rebuilding. Sommelle then lengthens your nights week after week.\n3. After 6 weeks: sleep is consolidated and you can put the diary away.
A program adapted for you
Based on your answers, Sommelle will not reduce your time in bed. Over 6 weeks, you will follow the morning diary, the night guidance and one exercise per week to calm your sleep.
Sommelle is not suited to your situation
Sommelle\'s method is designed for insomnia in adults. A doctor can offer you better-suited help.
Good to know
Start the program
Got it
Sommelle is designed for adults. Talk to your doctor about your sleep.
Snoring with pauses in breathing: talk to your doctor. It can be a sign of sleep apnea, which can be treated.
Falling asleep during the day: talk to your doctor. In the meantime, avoid driving if you feel drowsy.
Bipolar disorder: reducing time in bed can destabilize mood. Talk about your sleep with the doctor who follows you.
Epilepsy: lack of sleep can make seizures more likely. Talk about your sleep with the doctor who follows you.
Very late schedule: this may be a shift in your body clock rather than insomnia. A doctor can advise you.
Night or shift work: the standard program is not designed for this rhythm. An occupational health or sleep doctor can advise you.
In the first weeks, tiredness may increase. If you feel drowsy, do not drive or operate dangerous machinery.
When your nights are interrupted by someone else, the lack of sleep does not come from insomnia. Talk to your doctor if tiredness weighs on you.
During pregnancy, Sommelle will not reduce your time in bed.

If you are going through a hard time, please reach out now: call your local emergency number or a crisis line in your country, such as 988 in the United States. In France, 3114 is free, day and night, with trained people who listen.
Call 3114 (France)
A reminder each morning?
The program relies on your sleep diary: twenty seconds each morning. Sommelle can remind you after you wake up, and in the evening shortly before your sleep window starts.
You can change this at any time in the settings.
Yes, remind me
Not now
Notifications are turned off, so reminders will not appear. You can turn them on later in the settings.
